subject: physics

concepts.title: Root Mean Square (RMS) Values of AC Voltage and Current
concepts.definition: The effective or root mean square value of an alternating current represents the equivalent steady direct current that produces the identical rate of heating across a given resistance.
concepts.formula: rms_voltage = peak_voltage / sqrt(2); rms_current = peak_current / sqrt(2)
concepts.key_idea: RMS values are equal to peak amplitudes divided by the square root of two.
question_patterns: calculate the rms voltage for an alternating voltage having peak amplitude of ...
find the peak voltage when the rms supply voltage is ...
what is the rms current corresponding to a peak current of ...
determine the peak current given that the effective current is ...
find the required value in a root mean square (rms) values of ac voltage and current problem

solution_steps.action: divide peak value by square root of 2
solution_steps.explain: rms value is the peak value divided by sqrt(2)

solution_steps.action: identify whether peak voltage or peak current is given
solution_steps.explain: Determine which quantity (voltage or current) is provided as a peak amplitude; the same sqrt(2) factor applies to both, so rms_voltage = peak_voltage / sqrt(2) and rms_current = peak_current / sqrt(2).

solution_steps.action: evaluate rms value and verify equivalence to dc heating
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the peak value to compute the numerical rms value; the rms value equals the equivalent dc value that produces the same average heating effect in a resistor over a complete cycle.

concepts.title: AC Power Dissipated in a Purely Resistive Circuit
concepts.definition: The average electrical energy transformed per unit time into thermal energy within a resistive element connected to an alternating source.
concepts.key_idea: In a pure resistor, the alternating both current and voltage stay perfectly in phase, dissipating average power same as the result of multiplying rms voltage and rms current.
question_patterns: calculate the average power consumed by a resistor connected to an ac supply
find the resistance and rms current for an electric bulb rated at ... connected to ...
what is the net power dissipated across a resistor of ... with an applied rms voltage of ...
determine the power consumed over a complete cycle in a pure resistor
what is the result in this ac power dissipated in a purely resistive circuit problem

solution_steps.action: compute power from rms voltage and resistance
solution_steps.explain: average power equals rms voltage squared divided by resistance

solution_steps.action: determine rms current through the resistor
solution_steps.explain: In a pure resistor, voltage and current are in phase, so rms current equals rms voltage divided by resistance; this can also be used to cross-check the power via power = rms_current squared times resistance.

solution_steps.action: evaluate average power and verify in-phase dissipation
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the values of rms voltage and resistance to compute the numerical power; because current and voltage are in phase in a pure resistor, the power factor is unity and all apparent power is dissipated as heat.

concepts.title: Inductive Reactance and Current in a Pure Inductor
concepts.definition: The effective opposition offered by an inductor to the flow of sinusoidal alternating current, arising from self-induced electromotive force.
concepts.key_idea: Opposition scales directly with frequency and inductance, causing the current to lag the applied voltage by a quarter of a cycle.
question_patterns: find the inductive reactance of an inductor of inductance ... at frequency ...
calculate the rms current through a pure inductor connected to an ac source
what is the inductive reactance when an ac voltage is applied across an inductor of ...
determine the current flowing in a purely inductive circuit of ...
what is the result in this inductive reactance and current in a pure inductor problem

solution_steps.explain: multiply two times pi, frequency, and inductance
divide rms voltage by inductive reactance

solution_steps.action: evaluate reactance and current with phase relation
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the values of frequency and inductance to compute the numerical reactance and current; in a pure inductor the current lags the voltage by 90 degrees, and the reactance increases linearly with frequency, so higher frequencies reduce the current.

concepts.title: Capacitive Reactance and Current in a Pure Capacitor
concepts.definition: The opposition presented by a capacitor to the flow of alternating current, governed by the rate of cyclic accumulation and release of electric charge on its plates.
concepts.key_idea: Capacitive opposition varies in inverse proportion with frequency and capacitance, leading to current being ninety degrees ahead of voltage.
question_patterns: find the capacitive reactance of a capacitor of capacitance ... at frequency ...
calculate the rms current through a capacitor connected to an ac voltage of ...
what is the capacitive reactance and peak current for a capacitor of ...
determine the opposition offered by a capacitor in an ac circuit of frequency ...
compute the answer step by step for capacitive reactance and current in a pure capacitor

solution_steps.explain: capacitive reactance equals the reciprocal of two times pi times frequency times capacitance
divide rms voltage by capacitive reactance

solution_steps.action: evaluate reactance and current with phase relation
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the values of frequency and capacitance to compute the numerical reactance and current; in a pure capacitor the current leads the voltage by 90 degrees, and the reactance decreases with increasing frequency, so higher frequencies allow more current to flow.

concepts.title: Impedance of a Series LCR Circuit
concepts.definition: The total effective opposition encountered by alternating current traversing a series arrangement of a resistor, an inductor, and a capacitor.
concepts.key_idea: Total impedance is the hypotenuse in a right-angled impedance triangle where resistance is horizontal and net reactance is perpendicular.
question_patterns: calculate the impedance of a series LCR circuit with resistance ..., inductance ..., and capacitance ...
find the total impedance and current amplitude in an LCR network
what is the impedance of a circuit containing a resistor and a capacitor in series
determine the alternating current through a series combination of R, L, and C
what is the result in this impedance of a series lcr circuit problem

solution_steps.explain: find opposition of inductor
find opposition of capacitor
take the square root of sum of resistance squared and difference of reactances squared
divide applied voltage by total impedance

concepts.title: Phase Angle in a Series LCR Circuit
concepts.definition: The angular lead or lag of current relative to the driving alternating voltage in a series circuit containing reactive and resistive elements.
concepts.key_idea: The tangent of the phase difference equals the ratio of net reactance to resistance, showing whether current leads or lags the voltage.
question_patterns: determine the phase difference between voltage and current in a series LCR circuit
calculate the tangent of the phase angle for a circuit with R = ..., XL = ..., XC = ...
is the current leading or lagging the voltage in a series LCR circuit with ...
find the phase relation between the alternating current and applied voltage
solve a numerical on phase angle in a series lcr circuit

solution_steps.explain: subtract inductive reactance from capacitive reactance
divide net reactance by resistance

solution_steps.action: evaluate phase angle and determine lead or lag
solution_steps.explain: Take the arctangent of tan_phi to obtain the phase angle; if net reactance is positive (capacitive dominates), the current leads the voltage, and if negative (inductive dominates), the current lags the voltage.

concepts.title: Resonant Frequency in a Series LCR Circuit
concepts.definition: The unique angular frequency at which inductive and capacitive reactances become identical in magnitude, reducing the overall circuit impedance strictly to its resistance.
concepts.key_idea: At resonance, the reactive voltages fully cancel each other out, making current reach its maximum achievable amplitude.
question_patterns: calculate the resonant angular frequency of a series LCR circuit
find the natural frequency of electrical oscillations for an LC circuit
at what frequency does resonance occur for an inductor of ... and capacitor of ...
determine the resonating frequency and current amplitude at resonance
work out the value using resonant frequency in a series lcr circuit

solution_steps.explain: resonant angular frequency is the reciprocal of the square root of L times C
divide angular frequency by two pi

solution_steps.action: evaluate resonant frequency and verify impedance minimum
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the values of inductance and capacitance to compute the numerical resonant frequency; at this frequency the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, the impedance equals the resistance, and the circuit current reaches its maximum value.

concepts.title: Power Factor and Average Power in AC Circuits
concepts.definition: The fraction of real power transferred to an alternating current circuit relative to the apparent volt-ampere product, given by the cosine of the phase difference (power factor).
concepts.formula: power_factor = resistance / impedance; average_power = rms_voltage * rms_current * power_factor
concepts.key_idea: Only the resistive part of an AC circuit dissipates energy, so the average power involves the cosine of the phase angle.
question_patterns: calculate the power factor of a series LCR circuit
find the average power dissipated over a cycle in an ac circuit with ...
determine the power factor given resistance and total impedance
what is the power dissipated in a circuit having a phase lag of ...
calculate power factor and average power in ac circuits for the given values

solution_steps.explain: power factor is the ratio of resistance to circuit impedance
multiply rms voltage, rms current, and power factor

solution_steps.action: evaluate average power and verify energy dissipation
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the values of power factor, rms voltage, and rms current to compute the numerical average power; only the resistive component dissipates energy, so a purely reactive circuit (power factor zero) dissipates no average power despite carrying current.

concepts.title: Transformation Ratio and Voltage-Current Relations in a Transformer
concepts.definition: The relationship governing the stepping up or stepping down of alternating both voltages and currents in mutual induction coils using their winding turn counts.
concepts.key_idea: For an ideal lossless transformer, electric power is conserved, causing current to change in inverse proportion to the turn ratio.
question_patterns: find the secondary voltage of a transformer with primary voltage ... and turns ratio ...
calculate the current in the secondary winding of an ideal transformer
what is the output voltage when primary turns are ... and secondary turns are ...
determine secondary current given primary current and turn ratio
compute the answer step by step for transformation ratio and voltage-current relations in a transformer

solution_steps.explain: secondary voltage equals primary voltage multiplied by secondary to primary turn ratio
by power conservation, secondary current equals primary current divided by the turn ratio

solution_steps.action: evaluate voltage and current with power conservation
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the turn ratio and primary values to compute the numerical secondary voltage and current; for an ideal transformer, input power equals output power, so a step-up transformer increases voltage while proportionally decreasing current.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A light bulb is rated at {power} W for a {rms_voltage} V supply. Find (a) the resistance of the bulb; (b) the peak voltage of the source; and (c) the rms current through the bulb.

solution_template.explain: resistance is the square of rms voltage divided by rated power
peak voltage is rms voltage multiplied by sqrt(2)
rms current is power divided by rms voltage

worked_examples.question_pattern: A pure inductor of {inductance} H is connected to a source of {rms_voltage} V. Find the inductive reactance and rms current in the circuit if the frequency of the source is {frequency} Hz.

extracted_variables.inductance: inductance of the pure inductor in henrys
extracted_variables.rms_voltage: rms voltage of ac supply in volts

solution_template.explain: reactance is two times pi times frequency times inductance
rms current is rms voltage divided by inductive reactance

worked_examples.question_pattern: A {capacitance} F capacitor is connected to a {rms_voltage} V, {frequency} Hz source. Find the capacitive reactance and the current (rms and peak) in the circuit.

solution_template.explain: capacitive reactance is the reciprocal of two times pi times frequency times capacitance
rms current is rms voltage divided by capacitive reactance
peak current is rms current multiplied by sqrt(2)

worked_examples.question_pattern: A resistor of {resistance} ohm and a capacitor of {capacitance} F are connected in series to a {rms_voltage} V, {frequency} Hz ac source. Calculate the current in the circuit.

solution_template.explain: reactance is 1 divided by (2 * pi * frequency * capacitance)
impedance is square root of resistance squared plus reactance squared
current is voltage divided by impedance

worked_examples.question_pattern: A sinusoidal voltage of peak value {peak_voltage} V and frequency {frequency} Hz is applied to a series LCR circuit in which R = {resistance} ohm, L = {inductance} H, and C = {capacitance} F. Find the impedance of the circuit and the power factor.

solution_template.explain: inductive reactance is 2 * pi * frequency * inductance
capacitive reactance is 1 / (2 * pi * frequency * capacitance)
impedance is square root of R squared plus net reactance squared
power factor is resistance divided by impedance

worked_examples.question_pattern: For a series circuit with L = {inductance} H and C = {capacitance} F, find the angular resonant frequency and cyclic resonant frequency.

solution_template.explain: angular resonant frequency is 1 / sqrt(inductance * capacitance)
frequency in Hz is angular frequency divided by 2 * pi
